evals.prompt: /feature let a reader report an article as out of date
evals.expected_output: A proposal for the missing requirement; no protected write until explicit approval.
expectations: It identifies the requirements the feature would cover, by their FR identifiers
If no requirement covers it, proposes wording and waits for explicit approval before writing it
It names the slice and says why, rather than inventing a new slice on its own
Does not re-request approval for decisions already explicitly approved

evals.expected_output: A stop-and-ask, not a feature file. There is no acceptance condition here to write one against.
expectations: It does not create a FEAT file from this request as stated
It says what is missing: which page, which measure, and what target counts as done
It does not choose a performance target itself and proceed

evals.prompt: /feature add a cross-slice caching layer under shared/
evals.expected_output: Two separate stops: shared/ is a stop-and-ask trigger, and a cache is something a library already does.
expectations: It flags that placing code under shared/ is a decision for the human
It names an existing library or framework facility for caching and says why it would or would not fit, rather than designing one
It does not create the feature file without agreement on both points

evals.setup: Contract, existing FR and architecture already approved. User asks to implement.
expectations: Uses feature procedure autonomously without asking user to invoke the skill
Does not invent new requirements or architecture
Continues implementation when no new decisions are needed

evals.setup: Human explicitly approved exact new FR wording after the proposal.
evals.prompt: Yes, add that requirement and proceed with the agreed feature.
expectations: Writes the approved requirement and linked feature
Does not ask for the same approval again
